title: Teach someone the way
hook: hand on what you received, as Paul did
tomorrow: what do you sing when the whole journey is done?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Paul in Athens, a missionary disciple starting from a stranger's altar. The line was go, you are sent. Today, what he was sent with, and where he got it.
screen: `GO, YOU ARE SENT.` → `WHERE HE GOT IT.`

segments.voice: Nobody remembers learning to tie their shoes. Somebody knelt down, slowly, more than once, until the loop held. Prayers usually come the same way: a grandmother at bedtime, a parent in a car, a hand guiding your hand from forehead to chest. Paul has a line about this that holds an odd detail. Writing to Corinth about the Last Supper, he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you." Received of the Lord. But Paul wasn't at that supper. So who knelt down and showed him?
screen: `SOMEBODY KNELT DOWN AND SHOWED YOU.` → `RECEIVED OF THE LORD.` → `BUT PAUL WASN'T THERE.`

segments.voice: Readers answer the puzzle two ways. Some hear it as direct: Paul tells the Galatians he received the gospel by a revelation of Jesus Christ. Others hear it as a chain: the words came from the Lord, through those who were at the table, down to Paul. Either way, look at the two verbs. Received. Delivered. He uses them again a few chapters later, about the resurrection: "For I delivered unto you first of all, which I also received." Those are hand-to-hand words. Nobody in this picture invents the faith; each one takes it, and passes it along. Catholics call that living handing-on Tradition, and the Catechism describes it as the way the Church passes on all that she is and all that she believes, to every generation. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Last Supper reached the Corinthians the way your first prayer reached you, from somebody's hands. And now the chain has a spare link. Yours. Teaching the way doesn't mean a lecture. It can be one prayer, said slowly beside someone, the way it was said beside you.
screen: `A REVELATION, OR A CHAIN?` · `RECEIVED, DELIVERED.` · `THE CHURCH HANDS ON WHAT SHE IS.` · `THE CHAIN HAS A SPARE LINK.` · then, large: `HAND IT ON.`

segments.voice: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly, out loud, as if a child were copying you: forehead, chest, left shoulder, right. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Do it once more, slower, and let the sit hold the stillness after.
Teach someone the way. What Paul received, he delivered: one prayer, one person, hand to hand.
Carry this: hand it on, the way somebody once knelt down and showed you. Talk tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1787 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DO YOU SING WHEN THE JOURNEY IS DONE?`

howItsDone: Catholic parents, grandparents and godparents teach children the Sign of the Cross and first prayers at home; the Church calls the passing on of the faith Tradition.

fork.setup: your seven-year-old nephew asks how to pray, and you've got two minutes before his ride comes. what's the move Paul's verbs point to?
options: explain what prayer means first, so he understands.
pray one short prayer slowly beside him, and let him copy.
find him a kids' prayer video to watch later.
fork.reveal: received and delivered are hand-to-hand words. the faith reached Paul, and the Corinthians, from person to person; one prayer beside someone is the chain.

original.note: Greek: I handed on, I delivered. Paul's verb in 1 Corinthians 11:23 and 15:3.

chat.says: my cousin Lupe wants me to teach her Abuela's prayer before i go. where do i even start?
options: The way it came to you: one line at a time, said together, out loud.
Print it for her. Reading it alone is the fastest way to learn it.
Wait until she's older and can understand what every word means.
chat.meaning: Paul received and delivered: hand-to-hand words. A prayer usually reaches someone the way it reached you, said beside them.

Paul.meaning: the apostle whose letters fill much of the New Testament

Corinth.meaning: a Greek city where Paul founded a church

Last Supper.meaning: Jesus's final meal with his disciples before he died

Galatians.meaning: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia

Tradition.meaning: the Church's living handing-on of the faith

notes: 1 Corinthians 11:23, 15:3 and Matthew 28:19 quoted from Douay-Rheims (Challoner); confirm exact wording.

Two readings of 'received of the Lord' (direct revelation, cf. Galatians 1:12; or through the apostolic chain originating with the Lord): stated as 'readers answer two ways', ranking neither. Confirm.
CCC 78 paraphrased: through Tradition the Church perpetuates and transmits to every generation all that she herself is, all that she believes. Confirm.
Myth reveal: 'he wasn't one of the Twelve at the table' rests on Paul's own account of his call (Acts 9; 1 Corinthians 15:8–9). Confirm.
Trapdoor names the Greek verbs paralambano and paradidomi; the original game uses paredoka (1 Corinthians 11:23, 15:3). Confirm spelling and accents.
Shape: puzzle (Paul wasn't at the supper). Practice kind: say it out loud, with a gesture (the Sign of the Cross).
